correctness.rationale: Matrix strong-Markov decomposition is normalized by killed phase semigroup B=Lambda-Q, with F=B^{-1}(I-exp[-L sqrt(B/D)]), reset kernel F Lambda and finite positive success probability. The exact mean (h_L(B)-Q)^-1 1 follows, and symmetric-basis spectral inversion yields the two-eigenvalue formula. The small-distance coefficient is strictly positive by Jensen with spectral barycenter r; the large-distance ratio decays exponentially because b_-<r. Derivation proves all quantified parameters, not extrapolation from 432 independent numerical matrix-renewal checks and four backward-PDE discretizations; boundaries and lack of crossover uniqueness are explicit.

originality.rationale: The primary 2025 model paper explicitly suggests first-passage observables as an extension, and its stationary spatial laws contain no phase-retaining first-passage mean or comparison with constant hazard across target distance. The closest full-text treatment of switching diffusions uses a fixed reset intensity and resets the internal state, yielding a scalar renewal structure (Bressloff 2020, section 4). The age-dependent rate model of Pal-Kundu-Evans (2016) restarts its hazard after each reset, rather than preserving an autonomously switching phase. Actual semantic database queries and full-text comparisons found no specific stronger result implying this universal sign reversal; this supports qualified originality, not guaranteed first-publication priority.
residual_risks: An unindexed generic theorem for a Brownian searcher with persistent finite-state Markov-modulated resetting could subsume the new theorem despite the negative literature searches.

value.rationale: The motivating article explicitly identifies first-passage properties as an extension. For every nontrivial positive contrast and switching frequency at fixed mean reset intensity, the theorem supplies an exact, nonrenewal first-passage calculation and a structural sign reversal between nearby and distant targets. This is a physically interpretable search-efficiency result with a robust quantifier, rather than an arbitrary rate slice or formula re-expression; it motivates switching-rate design and experiment. No global best clock or unique crossing is claimed.
